business_problem: Booking.com needed to reduce the engineering burden and scalability risk of its self-managed Apache Kafka deployment as growing global demand increased the amount of streaming data behind booking and analytics workflows.
solution_summary: Booking.com replaced a self-managed Apache Kafka estate with Confluent Platform as the common streaming layer for individual business-unit clusters. The implementation shifts operational responsibility from homegrown cluster engineering to Confluent's enterprise-ready platform so teams can spend less time maintaining brokers and more time building customer-facing and analytical services. Streams that support Booking.com's booking experience are now managed with better reliability and built-in data-management capabilities, while governed data products on Confluent are shared with analysts plus finance and data-security teams. The same platform underpins connected-trip and personalization initiatives, where flight, accommodation, car-rental, and experience data can be combined more easily. Because the platform is cloud-native, the migration also gives Booking.com a clean runway for its next step: moving the streaming estate to the public cloud.

solution_components.name: Confluent Platform
solution_components.role: Runs Booking.com's enterprise streaming platform and replaces the company's self-managed Kafka clusters.

data_flow: Streaming data from Booking.com's business units flows through Confluent Platform instead of separate self-managed Kafka clusters, where it is governed into shared data products and consumed by analysts plus downstream connected-trip, personalization, finance, and data-security workloads.
business_outcome: Booking.com improved reliability, streamlined development, freed engineering resources for innovation, and created a governed streaming foundation for connected-trip, analytics, personalization, finance, and security use cases while preparing for public-cloud migration.
architecture_clues: Each Booking.com business unit transitioned its streaming clusters onto Confluent Platform.
The platform produces governed data products that are shared beyond engineering with finance and data-security teams.
Booking.com completed its move from open source Kafka to Confluent Platform before planning a later public-cloud migration.
